correct_answers: C) Decide what she needs before starting; put the request and the relevant material in the opening message; work through follow-ups that refer back to it; open a new chat for the next unrelated task.
explanations: Everything here is done before she has decided what she needs, so the opening message is assembled blind.
Opening a chat for the next task before the current one has been started puts the last step first.

Correct. Planning before starting, front-loading the material in one well-specified message, then building on it, is what keeps the exchange short; unrelated work starts fresh rather than dragging old context along.
Following up before the request has even been made, and deciding what is needed last, inverts the whole habit.
options: A) Put the request and the relevant material in the opening message; work through follow-ups that refer back to it; open a new chat for the next unrelated task; decide what she needs before starting.
B) Open a new chat for the next unrelated task; decide what she needs before starting; work through follow-ups that refer back to it; put the request and the relevant material in the opening message.
C) Decide what she needs before starting; put the request and the relevant material in the opening message; work through follow-ups that refer back to it; open a new chat for the next unrelated task.
